To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the practical predictability of tropical cyclones in the North Atlantic basin varies significantly with the synoptic flow regimes in which the genesis occurs and that the predictability is lower for the tropical transition (TT) pathways than for the non-TT pathways.

the predictability of tropical cyclone genesis over the North Atlantic basin is higher in some synoptic flow regimes than in others, and that the predictability in some regimes is linked to the lower predictive skill of the extratropical flow that influences the genesis environment.

the predictability of tropical cyclone formation is lower in synoptic flow regimes with stronger extratropical influence, and that the predictability can be largely explained by the predictability of the environmental state of the developing storm.

the predictability of the tropical cyclone formation over the North Atlantic basin in the GEFS is generally low, and the predictability is further reduced in the synoptic flow regimes associated with strong tropical transition and weak tropical transition pathways.
tropical cyclogenesis is a complex and difficult-to-predict phenomenon.
the predictability of tropical cyclone genesis in the North Atlantic basin is low in general.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tropical cyclogenesis predictability is low in the weak and strong TT pathways, and it is related to the low predictability of the environmental vertical wind shear and humidity.
the predictability of tropical cyclone genesis is strongly related to the strength of the synoptic-scale forcing and the associated environmental conditions.

the GEFS has a reasonable skill for tropical cyclogenesis in the North Atlantic basin, and the GEFS is more skillful than the GEFS ensemble mean in the nonbaroclinically induced genesis cases, which are more predictable than baroclinically or trough-induced genesis cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the predictability of tropical cyclone genesis over the North Atlantic varies with synoptic flow regimes.
the predictability of tropical cyclone genesis is highly sensitive to the environmental conditions in which it takes place.
tropical cyclones are more predictable in some flow regimes than others.
